flex_partition.name: Partition Numbers Flexibly
flex_partition.teaches: partitioning a 2-, 3- or 4-digit number in more than one way (45 = 40 + 5 = 30 + 15), with base-10 and part-whole models
flex_partition.representation: a part-whole diagram with one part given; base-10 picture beside it; write the other part

nl_20.name: Numbers on a Number Line (any scale)
nl_20.teaches: the number line as a counting and place-value tool: count along, find, place and estimate numbers on 0-20, 0-50, 0-100, 0-1,000, 0-10,000 and 0-1,000,000 lines, counting in 1s, 10s, 100s ... and with only some ticks labelled
nl_20.representation: a drawn number line with some ticks labelled; write the number at the arrow, or mark a number; option: scale; option: estimate on a line with only the ends marked

count_50s.name: Count in 50s, 100s and 1,000s (option)
count_50s.teaches: counting forwards and backwards in 50s, 100s and 1,000s, and seeing 10 hundreds as 1,000
count_50s.representation: step values 50, 100 and 1,000 on count_by_step_up / skip_count_line with a base-10 picture support

more_less_1_3digit.option: step 1 (1 more / 1 less) and a "1, 10 or 100" mix that stays within 1,000
more_less_1_3digit.name: Find 1, 10 or 100 More or Less (option)
more_less_1_3digit.teaches: finding 1, 10 or 100 more or less than a 3-digit number, including across a ten or hundred (399 + 1, 305 − 10)
more_less_1_3digit.representation: the existing frame cell "1 more than 489 is ____" with the place-value chart support; answer box
more_less_1_3digit.why: more_less_100 has steps 10, 100, 1,000 only; more_less_10 stops at 120

add_sub_patterns.name: Spot the Pattern (+/−)
add_sub_patterns.teaches: using known facts to add and subtract 1s, 10s and 100s (3 + 4, 30 + 40, 300 + 400) and seeing what changes and what stays the same
add_sub_patterns.representation: a three-row fact ladder with the first row done; complete the others

one_digit_addend.option: second number 1-digit (also on subtraction:sub_100_mixed): across a ten / not across
one_digit_addend.name: Add or Subtract Ones to a 2-Digit Number (option)
one_digit_addend.teaches: adding and subtracting a 1-digit number to or from a 2-digit number, first without and then across a ten (34 + 3, 34 − 3; 38 + 5, 42 − 5)
one_digit_addend.representation: one boxed cell per item: the across sentence with a base-10 picture (tens rods, ones cubes) under it as the structural support; answer box
one_digit_addend.why: the bands mix 1-digit + 1-digit and 2-digit + 2-digit; no option isolates 2-digit ± ones

tens_any.option: task: any multiple of 10 from a multiple of 10 (70 − 30), and a 2-digit number ± a multiple of 10 (34 + 20); support: tens rods
tens_any.name: Add and Subtract Multiples of Ten (option)
tens_any.teaches: adding and subtracting multiples of 10 (10-90) and adding a multiple of 10 to a 2-digit number, with rods, and relating it to the written sum

add_next_10.name: To the Next Ten
add_next_10.teaches: adding to reach the next multiple of 10 (38 + 2 = 40), then crossing it (38 + 5 = 38 + 2 + 3), and subtracting back to a ten (43 - 3)
add_next_10.representation: a number line with the ten marked; write the jump to the ten and then the rest

hundreds_any.option: task: any multiple of 100 to or from a 3-digit number (234 + 200, 650 − 300)
hundreds_any.name: Add and Subtract Hundreds (option)
hundreds_any.teaches: adding and subtracting multiples of 100 to and from 3-digit numbers, seeing only the hundreds digit change
hundreds_any.representation: equation cell with place-value counters (hundreds, tens, ones) drawn beside it as the structural support; answer box
hundreds_any.why: add_sub_100s deals only a hundred ± 100 (900 − 100); tens_any is the tens version

cross_100.name: Add and Subtract 10s Across 100 (option)
cross_100.teaches: adding or subtracting multiples of 10 across a hundred (180 + 30, 210 − 40)
cross_100.representation: a band option "tens across 100" with a number line support

exchange_count.option: exchanges: one in the ones / one in the tens / two or more (owner ruling 2026-10-10: on every regroup band, + − ×)
exchange_count.name: Number and Place of Exchanges (option)
exchange_count.teaches: column addition, subtraction and short multiplication with exactly one exchange (across a 10, or across a 100) before two or more, so each WRM step adds one new thing
exchange_count.representation: the existing column cell with its regroup boxes; the generator only picks operands with the chosen exchanges
exchange_count.why: the regroup bands mix exchange places and counts; WRM splits "across a 10" from "across a 100", and Y3.B4.S4 needs no exchange

two_and_three_digit.name: Add or Subtract a 2-Digit and a 3-Digit Number (option)
two_and_three_digit.teaches: adding a 2-digit number to a 3-digit number and subtracting a 2-digit number from a 3-digit number in columns, lining up the places
two_and_three_digit.representation: the column cell with the empty hundreds place of the 2-digit number shown, place headings H T O; answer boxes
two_and_three_digit.why: the 1k bands deal mostly 3-digit with 3-digit; lining up a shorter number is the step

bonds_100.name: Bonds to 100
bonds_100.teaches: pairs of tens that make 100 (30 + 70) and later any pair (37 + 63), from bonds to 10
bonds_100.representation: a hundred square or bead string with part shaded; part-whole diagram; write the missing part

make_decisions.name: Mental or Written?
make_decisions.teaches: choosing a mental strategy or the column method for a calculation, and explaining the choice
make_decisions.representation: a list of calculations; tick mental or written, then solve

multiples_2_5_10.name: Multiples of 2, 5 and 10 (option)
multiples_2_5_10.teaches: recognising multiples of 2, 5 and 10 (odd/even, ends in 0 or 5)
multiples_2_5_10.representation: a base option limited to 2, 5 and 10 with numbers to 100

tables_links.name: Related Times-Tables
tables_links.teaches: using one table to find another: 2 → 4 → 8 by doubling, 3 → 6 → 12, 5 and 10, and 9 as 10 − 1
tables_links.representation: a three-column table with the known table given; fill the doubled table

how_many_ways.name: How Many Ways?
how_many_ways.teaches: counting combinations systematically (3 tops × 4 bottoms) as a multiplication
how_many_ways.representation: a picture grid of items; list or draw every pair; write the multiplication

metres.name: Measure in Metres (option)
metres.teaches: measuring and comparing lengths in metres, choosing cm or m
metres.representation: a metre stick picture; unit choice cm/m

mm_cm_m.name: Metres, Centimetres, Millimetres (option)
mm_cm_m.teaches: measuring in mm, cm and m and converting between them (2 m 30 cm = 230 cm)
mm_cm_m.representation: ruler pictures in mm; mixed-unit answers (_ m _ cm)

ruler_cm.name: Read a Centimetre Ruler (option)
ruler_cm.teaches: measuring lengths in whole centimetres, then millimetres, on a metric ruler (the skill reads inches only)
ruler_cm.representation: a unit option (cm, mm) on reading_ruler with the same arrow-and-ruler picture

length_ops.name: Length Word Problems
length_ops.teaches: adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing lengths and heights in context (same units)
length_ops.representation: a drawn ruler or bar model with the lengths labelled; write the answer with its unit

compare_lengths.name: Compare Lengths
compare_lengths.teaches: comparing and ordering lengths in mixed units (1 m 20 cm vs 125 cm)
compare_lengths.representation: two labelled bars; write <, > or = after converting

add_sub_lengths.name: Add and Subtract Lengths
add_sub_lengths.teaches: adding and subtracting lengths in the same and mixed units, including bar-model "longer by" / "shorter by" problems
add_sub_lengths.representation: a bar model with two lengths; write the total or the difference with the unit

fraction_parts.name: Equal and Unequal Parts
fraction_parts.teaches: parts and wholes; deciding whether parts are equal; finding the whole from a part
fraction_parts.representation: shapes split into parts; tick equal / not equal; draw the whole from a half or a quarter

frac_count.name: Count in Fractions
frac_count.teaches: counting up and down in unit fractions on a number line and past a whole (1/4, 2/4, 3/4, 1, 1 1/4)
frac_count.representation: a number line with fraction ticks; fill the missing counts

compare_kind.option: kind: unit fractions / same denominator / same numerator (also on order_fractions)
compare_kind.name: Compare Unit or Same-Denominator Fractions (option)
compare_kind.teaches: comparing and ordering unit fractions (1/3 > 1/5: more parts, smaller part) and fractions with the same denominator (2/5 < 4/5)
compare_kind.representation: two bar models of the same whole length, one under the other, with the sign box between; ordering cell with 3 fractions
compare_kind.why: compare mixes every kind of pair; WRM teaches unit fractions, then same denominators, as separate steps

frac_whole.name: Understand the Whole
frac_whole.teaches: how many parts of a given size make a whole (4/4 = 1), and finding the whole from a part
frac_whole.representation: a bar split into parts with some shaded; write how many more make the whole

frac_scales.name: Fractions and Scales
frac_scales.teaches: reading a scale or number line divided into halves, quarters, fifths and tenths of a unit
frac_scales.representation: a measuring scale (jug, ruler, number line) with unlabelled intervals; write the reading as a fraction

nonstandard_mass.name: Measure Mass with Cubes
nonstandard_mass.teaches: measuring mass with non-standard units (cubes, marbles) on a balance, and comparing masses by the count
nonstandard_mass.representation: a drawn balance with an object in one pan and cubes in the other; write how many cubes

mass_scales.name: Read Scales (g, kg, ml, l)
mass_scales.teaches: reading mass and capacity scales in grams, kilograms, millilitres and litres with scale steps of 1, 2, 5, 10, 100
mass_scales.representation: a drawn dial or jug scale; write the reading with the unit; option: scale step

mass_ops.name: Mass and Capacity Word Problems
mass_ops.teaches: adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing masses and capacities in context
mass_ops.representation: picture of scales/jugs with values; write the answer with the unit

metric_mass_capacity.option: metric whole and mixed units without decimals: kg ↔ g and l ↔ ml (2 kg = 2,000 g; 1 l 500 ml = 1,500 ml)
metric_mass_capacity.name: Equivalent Masses and Capacities (option)
metric_mass_capacity.teaches: converting kilograms and grams, litres and millilitres, using 1 kg = 1,000 g and 1 l = 1,000 ml and number bonds to 1,000
metric_mass_capacity.representation: conversion cell "1 kg 250 g = ____ g" with a part-whole bar (1,000 + 250); answer box
metric_mass_capacity.why: unit_conversions is customary only (ounces, pounds); capacity converts L/mL with decimals (1.5 L) and has no mass

compare_measures.name: Compare Masses and Capacities
compare_measures.teaches: comparing two masses or capacities given in g and kg, ml and l (450 g < 1 kg; 1,200 ml > 1 l) with <, > and =, and ordering three
compare_measures.representation: two measurement labels (or two drawn scales) with a sign box between; same-unit first, then mixed units
compare_measures.why: mass_ops is the four operations; heavier_lighter_visual compares pictures without units

nonstandard_capacity.name: Measure Capacity with Cups
nonstandard_capacity.teaches: measuring capacity and volume with non-standard units (cups, spoons) and comparing
nonstandard_capacity.representation: containers with a count of cups drawn beside them; write how many cups; circle the one that holds more

capacity_early.name: Full, Empty, Holds More
capacity_early.teaches: capacity language (full, empty, half full, nearly full) and comparing how much two containers hold
capacity_early.representation: outline containers with a drawn fill line; circle full/empty or the one that holds more; option: order three

within_whole.option: sums within one whole (no answer above 1)
within_whole.name: Add Fractions Within a Whole (option)
within_whole.teaches: adding fractions with the same denominator whose total is at most one whole (2/5 + 1/5 = 3/5)
within_whole.representation: the existing bar-model add cell; answer: numerator over the given denominator
within_whole.why: the skill deals sums past 1 (4/5 + 2/5 = 1 1/5), which is Y4

frac_whole_partition.name: Partition the Whole
frac_whole_partition.teaches: finding the fraction that completes a whole (1 − 3/5), as a part-whole or bar model
frac_whole_partition.representation: a bar model with one part given as a fraction; write the missing part

single_fraction.option: fraction: one chosen fraction (1/2, 1/4, 3/4, 1/3, 2/4) instead of a denominator family; also on identify, write_fraction, equiv_frac_visual, fraction_of_set
single_fraction.name: One Fraction per Page (option)
single_fraction.teaches: a page about ONE fraction (find a quarter, find a third, three-quarters) of a shape and of an amount, as WRM Y2 teaches them one at a time
single_fraction.representation: the existing fraction cells (area, bar, circle, set of objects) with the one fraction; answer: shade or write the number
single_fraction.why: `denoms` picks a family (halves → quarters, eighths); WRM Y2 needs one fraction per step

frac_amount_wp.name: Fraction of an Amount Problems
frac_amount_wp.teaches: reasoning about fractions of amounts with a bar model: find a part, find the whole, compare two fractions of amounts
frac_amount_wp.representation: a bar model split into equal parts with the whole or a part labelled; write the missing value

money_notes.name: Recognise Notes (option)
money_notes.teaches: recognising banknotes and their values alongside coins (the school teaches US dollars)
money_notes.representation: add notes to the coin-value picture bank

money_convert.name: Dollars and Cents (option)
money_convert.teaches: converting between cents and dollars-and-cents (345 cents = $3.45) and recording money
money_convert.representation: option: cents to dollars and back

money_difference.option: op "difference": subtract two prices / find how much more
money_difference.name: Difference Between Two Amounts (option)
money_difference.teaches: finding the difference between two amounts of money (a $7 toy and a $15 toy: $8 more), by counting on or subtracting
money_difference.representation: two price tags in one cell, the sentence "___ − ___ = ___" with a bar model support; answer box with the $ sign printed
money_difference.why: measurement:money only adds prices; money_change finds change from a whole amount, not a difference

time_talk.name: Time Words
time_talk.teaches: the language of time (today, yesterday, tomorrow, days of the week, months, seasons, before, after)
time_talk.representation: calendar strip or picture timeline; circle or write the word from a bank

roman_12.name: Roman Numerals to 12
roman_12.teaches: reading Roman numerals I to XII on a clock face
roman_12.representation: a clock face with Roman numerals; write the time or the numeral value

time_facts.name: Minutes, Hours and Days
time_facts.teaches: knowing and using 60 minutes in an hour, 24 hours in a day, 7 days in a week, and converting simple times
time_facts.representation: fact cells with a clock or timeline support; option: word problems

day_order.name: First, Next, Then
day_order.teaches: sequencing events and times of day (morning, afternoon, evening, night; before, after; first, next, then)
day_order.representation: three or four picture cards; number them 1-4 in order; option: before/after questions

time_calendar.name: Years, Months, Days, Hours
time_calendar.teaches: converting and comparing units of time: years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds; days in each month; leap years
time_calendar.representation: a calendar page or conversion table; fill the missing values

time_units.name: Hours, Minutes or Seconds?
time_units.teaches: a sense of time units: which activities take seconds, minutes or hours
time_units.representation: activity pictures with a unit word bank; option: longer/shorter

shape_sort.name: Sort 2-D and 3-D Shapes
shape_sort.teaches: sorting shapes by one property (sides, corners, flat or curved faces, rolls or stacks) and naming the sorting rule
shape_sort.representation: shape tiles and two labelled sorting rings or a Carroll-style two-box table

turns_angles.name: Turns and Angles
turns_angles.teaches: an angle as an amount of turn; right angles as quarter turns; comparing angles with a right angle (greater/less)
turns_angles.representation: an angle tester (a square corner) beside each angle; tick greater, less or right angle

shape_draw.name: Draw 2-D Shapes
shape_draw.teaches: drawing 2-D shapes on a dot grid from a name or a description (4 sides, 2 long and 2 short)
shape_draw.representation: a square dot grid; draw the shape; the key shows one correct drawing

draw_measure.name: Measure and Draw Accurately
draw_measure.teaches: measuring lines to the nearest cm/mm and drawing lines of a given length
draw_measure.representation: a ruler picture under a line; option: draw a line of 7 cm on the grid (key shows the length)

hv_lines.name: Horizontal and Vertical Lines
hv_lines.teaches: recognising horizontal and vertical lines in shapes and on a grid
hv_lines.representation: shapes with sides marked; write H or V for each marked line

make_3d.name: Make 3-D Shapes
make_3d.teaches: making skeleton 3-D shapes (straws and balls) and matching nets or faces to shapes
make_3d.representation: a picture of a skeleton model; write how many straws and balls; option: match a net

pictogram_scale.name: Pictograms with a Key (option)
pictogram_scale.teaches: drawing pictograms where one picture stands for 2, 5 or 10, including half pictures

block_diagram.name: Block Diagrams
block_diagram.teaches: reading and drawing block diagrams (one square = one) with a scale in 1s or 2s
block_diagram.representation: a squared grid with labelled columns; count the blocks or colour to build

table_data.name: Tables
table_data.teaches: reading and completing simple tables and tally-to-number tables
table_data.representation: a two-column table with blanks; fill in the counts; answer one question

collect_data.name: Collect and Represent Data
collect_data.teaches: collecting data into a tally, then choosing a table, pictogram or bar chart to show it
collect_data.representation: a list of raw data; tally it, then draw the chart on a grid

two_way.name: Two-Way Tables
two_way.representation: a two-way table with blanks and totals; fill them in
